# Authentication & Auto-Start Setup Guide Everything needed to deploy the X3 Chain authentication swarm and auto-start stack. This guide covers systemd-based service orchestration, credential hardening, JWT security, and service health checks. ## Quick Start ### 1. Install Systemd Services (auto-start on boot) ```bash sudo bash /home/lojak/Desktop/x3-chain-master/deployment/scripts/install-services.sh ``` This script provisions an `x3` service user, places three unit files under systemd control, and enables them for boot-time activation. **Services installed (swarm of core processes):** - `redis.service` — Cache and session store on port 6379 - `ccgv-validator.service` — Cross-chain GPU validator on port 8000 - `x3-intelligence.service` — Dashboard with authentication on port 5173 ### 2. Create Configuration File ```bash cp deployment/env/.env.template .env nano .env ``` **Critical environment variables:** - `AUTH_SALT` — Salt for password hashing to prevent rainbow-table attacks - `JWT_SECRET` — Secret for signing JSON Web Tokens - `REDIS_HOST` — Host for session persistence (default `localhost`) - `CCGV_RPC_ETHEREUM` — Ethereum RPC endpoint (e.g., Alchemy) - `CCGV_RPC_SOLANA` — Solana RPC endpoint ### 3. Change Default Credentials Edit `apps/x3-intelligence/src/auth.ts` to replace the demo password and set a strong `AUTH_SALT`. Rebuild the dashboard to apply changes. ```typescript // Find the login validation section (around line 23) const DEFAULT_USERS = [ { id: '1', username: 'admin', password: hashPassword('YOUR-NEW-PASSWORD'), email: 'admin@example.com' } ]; // Also update AUTH_SALT for better security const AUTH_SALT = process.env.AUTH_SALT || 'your-secure-random-salt'; ``` Rebuild: ```bash cd /home/lojak/Desktop/x3-chain-master/apps/x3-intelligence npm install npm run build ``` ## Architecture ### Authentication Flow (swarm of checks) ``` User Login (LoginPage.tsx) ↓ authService.login() - POST /api/auth/login ↓ Backend validates credentials (auth.ts) ↓ JWT token issued (24hr expiry) ↓ Token stored in localStorage ↓ ProtectedRoute checks authentication ↓ Dashboard accessible ``` ### Components & Files #### Frontend - **LoginPage.tsx** — UI for credential entry - **AppBar.tsx** — Navigation bar with user menu and logout - **ProtectedRoute.tsx** — Wrapper enforcing authentication - **useAuth.ts** — React hook for auth state management - **authService.ts** — API client and token handling #### Backend - **auth.ts** — Endpoints, password verification, JWT issuance - **env template** — Environment variable definitions #### Infrastructure - **ccgv-validator.service** — Validator service - **x3-intelligence.service** — Dashboard service - **redis.service** — Redis cache and sessions - **install-services.sh** — Installer for systemd units - **startup.sh** — Manual startup fallback ## How to Use ### Login 1. Navigate to http://localhost:5173. 2. Enter credentials: - Username: `admin` - Password: `x3-chain-2026` 3. Click **Sign In** to reach the dashboard. ### Logout 1. Click your username in the top-right corner. 2. Select **Logout** to clear session data. ### Change Password 1. Open the user menu. 2. Select **Change Password**. 3. Provide current and new passwords, then confirm. ## Integration with Your App ### Using the `useAuth` Hook ```typescript import { useAuth } from '@/hooks/useAuth'; function MyComponent() { const { user, isAuthenticated, logout, login } = useAuth(); return (
{isAuthenticated &&

Welcome, {user?.username}!

}
); } ``` **Why it works:** `useAuth` centralizes authentication state, ensuring any component can read the active user, enforce access, and trigger logout across the swarm of protected views. ### Protecting Routes ```typescript import { ProtectedRoute } from '@/components/ProtectedRoute'; import Dashboard from '@/pages/Dashboard'; } /> } /> ``` **Why it works:** `ProtectedRoute` intercepts navigation, checks token presence and validity, and redirects unauthenticated users before rendering secure pages. ### Making Authenticated API Calls ```typescript const { getAuthHeader } = useAuth(); const fetchDashboardData = async () => { const response = await fetch('/api/dashboard', { headers: getAuthHeader() }); const data = await response.json(); return data; }; ``` **Why it works:** `getAuthHeader` injects the current JWT into the `Authorization` header, allowing the backend to validate the caller within the service swarm. ## Service Management ### Check Service Status ```bash # Check if services are running sudo systemctl status redis.service sudo systemctl status ccgv-validator.service sudo systemctl status x3-intelligence.service # View logs for a service sudo journalctl -u x3-intelligence.service -n 50 sudo journalctl -u ccgv-validator.service -n 50 sudo journalctl -u redis.service -n 50 # Follow logs in real-time sudo journalctl -u x3-intelligence.service -f ``` ### Start/Stop Services Manually ```bash # Start individual service sudo systemctl start x3-intelligence.service # Stop individual service sudo systemctl stop x3-intelligence.service # Restart service sudo systemctl restart x3-intelligence.service # Enable/disable auto-start sudo systemctl enable x3-intelligence.service sudo systemctl disable x3-intelligence.service ``` ### Fallback: Manual Startup If systemd is unavailable, use the startup script: ```bash bash deployment/scripts/startup.sh ``` This launches Redis, CCGV validator, and X3 Intelligence in a lightweight swarm, matching the same ports as the managed units. ## Testing Authentication ### Manual Login Test ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:5173/api/auth/login \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"username":"admin","password":"x3-chain-2026"}' ``` Expected response: ```json { "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...", "user": { "id": "1", "username": "admin", "email": "admin@example.com" }, "expiresIn": 86400 } ``` ### Validate Token ```bash curl -X GET http://localhost:5173/api/auth/validate \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" ``` ## Token Validation Tokens are checked at login, on protected routes, during API requests, and refreshed to extend sessions by 24 hours. The swarm of checks minimizes unauthorized access. ## Sessions & Storage - Frontend stores tokens in `localStorage`. - Backend keeps session data in memory or Redis when configured. - Default expiry is 24 hours, with optional refresh via `/api/auth/refresh`. ## Security Features - JWT tokens with 24-hour expiry - Password hashing with SHA-256 plus salt - CORS headers on all responses - Planned HTTP-only cookie support - Token validation on each protected request - Logout flow clears all session artifacts across the swarm of services ## Troubleshooting ### "Connection failed. Is the server running?" ```bash curl http://localhost:8000 sudo lsof -i :8000 bash deployment/scripts/startup.sh ``` ### "Invalid credentials" on known-good password - Ensure `.env` `AUTH_SALT` matches the backend configuration. - Confirm default credentials were not altered unintentionally. - Inspect backend logs with `journalctl`. ### Default credentials aren't working - Verify the admin user exists in `auth.ts`. - Confirm hashing logic aligns with the configured salt. - Restart with the startup script if needed. ### Services won't start on boot ```bash sudo systemctl list-unit-files | grep x3 sudo systemctl enable x3-intelligence.service sudo journalctl -xe ``` ## Production Checklist - [ ] Change default admin password - [ ] Set strong `AUTH_SALT` and `JWT_SECRET` - [ ] Configure valid RPC endpoints - [ ] Point `REDIS_HOST` to the desired instance - [ ] Enable HTTPS for the login surface - [ ] Enable Redis persistence (append-only) - [ ] Configure log rotation for X3 services - [ ] Test failover and recovery - [ ] Audit password storage and token handling - [ ] Add monitoring for service health and swarm availability ## Architecture Diagram The architecture runs as a coordinated swarm of services: browser clients call the frontend, which uses `authService` to request JWTs from the backend; Redis maintains session state; systemd keeps Redis, the validator, and the dashboard online via supervised units. Protected routes enforce token checks before rendering authenticated content. ## File Structure ``` x3-chain-master/ ├── apps/x3-intelligence/src/ │ ├── components/ │ ├── services/ │ ├── hooks/ │ └── auth.ts ├── deployment/ │ ├── systemd/ │ ├── scripts/ │ └── env/ └── cross-chain-gpu-validator/ ``` ## Next Steps 1. Install services. 2. Configure environment variables. 3. Change credentials and salt. 4. Test login at http://localhost:5173. 5. Set up monitoring and alerts. 6. Follow the production hardening checklist. ## Resources - [systemd](https://systemd.io) - [systemctl reference](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/systemctl.html) - [journalctl reference](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/journalctl.html) - [Redis](https://redis.io) - [JSON Web Tokens](https://jwt.io) - [React](https://react.dev) - [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org) - [npm](https://www.npmjs.com) - [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) - [cURL](https://curl.se) - [Alchemy Ethereum RPC](https://www.alchemy.com) - [Solana RPC Endpoints](https://docs.solana.com/cluster/rpc-endpoints)
